title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
This record is the current public workflow and replication packet for the Modern LaTeX Manuscripts project. It describes the actual AI-run process now being used: local source intake, scan/OCR/VLM witness generation, TeX reconstruction, mathematical translation, source-image and object-level auditing, web/pro review handoffs, conservative status labelling, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Read first: 00_AI_Run_Modern_LaTeX_Manuscript_Workflow_Current_20260706.pdf. That PDF is the front-facing workflow summary. The Markdown source and the ZIP contain supporting addenda, scripts, logs, and cleanup notes.

Important status rule. This workflow record is not a critical edition, not proof that any author corpus is complete, and not a certification layer. OCR output, VLM readings, formula crops, first-pass TeX, object detectors, and web-run transcripts are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Public author records should distinguish OCR-derived TeX, working drafts, source-witnessed tranches, and critically checked editions.

Current lesson. The most reliable pattern is source-first and reader-first: front the PDF or reader a human wants to inspect, put TeX/source/audit/provenance in coherent ZIPs, keep file counts low, use high-resolution scans/crops for hard mathematics and diagrams, use OCR as a prose-completeness witness rather than authority, compile/render-check everything, and publish conservative caveats rather than completion claims.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections and reproducibility improvements can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Human-readable cleanup of the workflow DOI. Replaces the accumulated loose-addendum surface with a front PDF/Markdown workflow summary plus a supporting ZIP of prior addenda, scripts, and cleanup logs.
